headlines.text: Your crew opens it and goes

payload.hypothesis: Control leads with the switch itself. This one leads with the proof of why a switch sticks: the crew opens it, there is nothing to learn, and the price is said out loud instead of quoted after a demo.

descriptions.text: Crews quit software they cannot use. OPS opens to today's jobs. No manual.
It works offline. A dead signal in a basement does not stop the job.
Nothing held back on the cheap tier. $90 a month, $140 when the crew grows.

proposal.rationale: COMPETITOR is the most expensive line we run: $451.47 in 28 days, and the only paying customer this account has ever produced came out of it at $340.20. That buys the ad group a better ad, not a pause. The control is 39 days old and leads with the switch itself, which is the same thing every comparison page says. This one leads with the reason a switch sticks: crews quit software they cannot use, and that is the whole reason OPS exists. It says the price out loud on a page where the competition asks you to book a demo first, and it names the crew size we actually serve instead of pretending we serve everyone. One competitor mention, in the approved form, in the only campaign allowed to carry it.
